quests.hint: Listen carefully for which family member is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Brother' refers to a male sibling; 'sister' refers to a female sibling. These are among the most common family words in English - listen for them carefully.
quests.textToSpeak: My brother plays football after school.
quests.correctAnswer: My sister plays football after school.

quests.hint: Focus on what she is eating for breakfast.
quests.explanation: 'Bread' is uncooked sliced loaf; 'toast' is bread that has been heated until brown and crispy. Both are breakfast staples - a useful vocabulary pair to know.
quests.textToSpeak: She eats bread for breakfast every morning.
quests.correctAnswer: She eats toast for breakfast every morning.

quests.hint: Notice which animal is sleeping on the sofa.
quests.explanation: 'Dog' and 'cat' are the two most common pets in English-speaking countries. Both are short words, so listen carefully - 'dog' has the 'd' sound, 'cat' has the 'c' sound.
quests.textToSpeak: The dog sleeps on the sofa every night.
quests.correctAnswer: The cat sleeps on the sofa every night.

quests.hint: Pay attention to the time he wakes up.
quests.explanation: 'Six' and 'seven' can sound similar in fast speech. Numbers are often the most important information in a sentence - always listen for them carefully.
quests.textToSpeak: He wakes up at six o'clock every day.
quests.correctAnswer: He wakes up at seven o'clock every day.

quests.hint: Listen for which drink is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Coffee' and 'tea' are the two most popular hot drinks in English-speaking countries. 'Coffee' has two syllables (COF-fee); 'tea' has only one. Listen for the difference.
quests.textToSpeak: I drink coffee every morning before work.
quests.correctAnswer: I drink tea every morning before work.

quests.hint: Focus on the time word at the end of the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Early' and 'late' are opposites. 'Early' means before the usual or expected time; 'late' means after it. These common adverbs appear in hundreds of everyday sentences.
quests.textToSpeak: She always goes to bed early on weekdays.
quests.correctAnswer: She always goes to bed late on weekdays.

quests.hint: Listen for the food they eat for lunch.
quests.explanation: 'Soup' is a liquid dish; 'pasta' is an Italian dish made from dough. Both are popular lunches. Building food vocabulary is essential for everyday conversations in English.
quests.textToSpeak: We usually have soup for lunch on weekdays.
quests.correctAnswer: We usually have pasta for lunch on weekdays.

quests.hint: Notice which type of juice he drinks.
quests.explanation: Both 'orange juice' and 'apple juice' end in 'juice', so listen carefully for the first word. In compound nouns, the first word usually carries the most important meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: He likes orange juice with his breakfast.
quests.correctAnswer: He likes apple juice with his breakfast.

quests.hint: Listen for what the children eat as a treat.
quests.explanation: 'Ice cream' is a frozen dessert; 'chocolate' is a sweet made from cocoa. Notice that 'ice cream' is two words while 'chocolate' is one - details like this matter in English spelling.
quests.textToSpeak: The children eat ice cream after dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: The children eat chocolate after dinner.

quests.hint: Focus on the type of home she lives in.
quests.explanation: In British English, a 'flat' is an apartment inside a building; a 'house' is a standalone building. This is an important vocabulary difference between American and British English.
quests.textToSpeak: She lives in a small flat near the centre.
quests.correctAnswer: She lives in a small house near the centre.

quests.hint: Listen for where he works.
quests.explanation: 'Hospital' and 'school' are both important community buildings, but very different. Listening for key nouns tells you the context of the whole sentence immediately.
quests.textToSpeak: He works in a hospital near the city.
quests.correctAnswer: He works in a school near the city.

quests.hint: Notice the adjective describing the kitchen.
quests.explanation: 'Clean' means free from dirt; 'tidy' means neatly organised. A room can be clean but untidy, or tidy but not clean - these are useful words to distinguish in everyday life.
quests.textToSpeak: The kitchen is very clean after dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: The kitchen is very tidy after dinner.

quests.hint: Pay attention to the colour of the dress.
quests.explanation: 'Red' and 'blue' are basic colour adjectives. In English, colours come directly before the noun they describe. Colours are among the most frequently used adjectives in conversation.
quests.textToSpeak: She bought a red dress for the party.
quests.correctAnswer: She bought a blue dress for the party.

quests.hint: Listen for the length of his hair.
quests.explanation: 'Short' and 'long' are opposite adjectives used for hair, distances, films, and much more. They appear constantly in everyday English and are essential vocabulary to master.
quests.textToSpeak: He has short black hair and brown eyes.
quests.correctAnswer: He has long black hair and brown eyes.

quests.hint: Focus on the adverb describing how the man walks.
quests.explanation: 'Slowly' describes the speed of movement; 'carefully' describes the level of attention or caution. Both are adverbs ending in '-ly', but they mean very different things.
quests.textToSpeak: The old man walks slowly through the park.
quests.correctAnswer: The old man walks carefully through the park.

quests.hint: Listen for what type of weather is happening.
quests.explanation: 'Raining' and 'snowing' are both weather verbs describing precipitation. Rain is liquid water; snow is frozen. Both use the '-ing' form with 'is' to describe current weather.
quests.textToSpeak: It is raining heavily outside right now.
quests.correctAnswer: It is snowing heavily outside right now.

quests.hint: Notice the word that describes the temperature.
quests.explanation: 'Cold' and 'hot' are opposites on the temperature scale. In everyday English, we say 'It is cold today' or 'It is hot today'. These simple adjectives are used constantly in conversation.
quests.textToSpeak: The weather is very cold this morning.
quests.correctAnswer: The weather is very hot this morning.

quests.hint: Focus on what she carries when it rains.
quests.explanation: An 'umbrella' is held over your head to block rain; a 'raincoat' is waterproof clothing you wear. Both protect against rain but in different ways - useful everyday vocabulary.
quests.textToSpeak: She always carries an umbrella when it rains.
quests.correctAnswer: She always carries a raincoat when it rains.

quests.hint: Listen for the verb that describes the teacher's action.
quests.explanation: 'Writes' means forming words or letters; 'draws' means making pictures or diagrams. Both are classroom actions. Distinguishing action verbs in context is a key listening skill.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher writes on the board every lesson.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher draws on the board every lesson.

quests.hint: Pay attention to which school subject is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Maths' and 'English' are both core school subjects. In British English, the school subject is called 'Maths' (not 'Math'). Listen for these subject names in sentences about school life.
quests.textToSpeak: She studies maths for two hours every evening.
quests.correctAnswer: She studies English for two hours every evening.

quests.hint: Notice what the students are doing in the library.
quests.explanation: 'Read books' and 'write notes' are both study activities. Reading is a receptive skill (taking in information); writing is a productive skill (creating output). Both are key in learning English.
quests.textToSpeak: Students read books quietly in the library.
quests.correctAnswer: Students write notes quietly in the library.

quests.hint: Listen for what he buys at the market.
quests.explanation: 'Vegetables' are savoury plant foods (carrots, beans, potatoes); 'fruit' is typically sweet (apples, oranges, bananas). Both are bought fresh at markets - a common shopping vocabulary topic.
quests.textToSpeak: He buys fresh vegetables at the local market.
quests.correctAnswer: He buys fresh fruit at the local market.

quests.hint: Focus on how she pays in the shop.
quests.explanation: 'Credit card' and 'cash' are both payment methods. In modern English, you 'pay by card' or 'pay in cash'. This is essential vocabulary for shopping situations in English-speaking countries.
quests.textToSpeak: She always pays with a credit card in the shop.
quests.correctAnswer: She always pays with cash in the shop.

quests.hint: Pay attention to the price of the bag.
quests.explanation: 'Twenty' and 'thirty' both end in '-ty' and can sound very similar at speed. Learning to distinguish numbers ending in '-ty' from '-teen' (e.g., thirty vs thirteen) is a vital listening skill.
quests.textToSpeak: The bag costs twenty dollars at that shop.
quests.correctAnswer: The bag costs thirty dollars at that shop.

quests.hint: Listen for the type of transport he uses.
quests.explanation: 'Bus' and 'train' are both forms of public transport. A bus travels on roads; a train travels on tracks. These common transport nouns appear frequently in everyday English conversations.
quests.textToSpeak: I take the bus to work every day.
quests.correctAnswer: I take the train to work every day.

quests.hint: Notice how many minutes the taxi takes.
quests.explanation: 'Ten' and 'five' are both small numbers. In English, time expressions like 'in ten minutes' or 'in five minutes' are very common. Always listen carefully for the number - it changes the meaning completely.
quests.textToSpeak: The taxi will arrive in ten minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: The taxi will arrive in five minutes.

quests.hint: Focus on which vehicle he rides to school.
quests.explanation: A 'bicycle' is powered by pedalling; a 'motorbike' has an engine. Both are two-wheeled vehicles but very different. Learning vehicle vocabulary is important for talking about transport and travel.
quests.textToSpeak: He rides his bicycle to school every morning.
quests.correctAnswer: He rides his motorbike to school every morning.

quests.hint: Listen for what they enjoy watching at weekends.
quests.explanation: 'Films' are movies you watch; 'sport' refers to athletic events. Both are popular leisure activities. 'Watch films' and 'watch sport' are very common English phrases for describing free time.
quests.textToSpeak: They love watching films on the weekends.
quests.correctAnswer: They love watching sport on the weekends.

quests.hint: Pay attention to what type of reading material she enjoys.
quests.explanation: 'Novels' are long fictional books; 'magazines' are shorter publications with articles on various topics. Both are reading materials. 'I like reading...' is a very common phrase for expressing hobbies.
quests.textToSpeak: She likes reading novels in her free time.
quests.correctAnswer: She likes reading magazines in her free time.

quests.hint: Focus on which musical instrument he plays.
quests.explanation: 'Guitar' is a string instrument played by strumming; 'piano' is a keyboard instrument. Both are very popular. Musical instrument names are common in conversations about hobbies and interests.
quests.textToSpeak: He plays guitar in a band on weekends.
quests.correctAnswer: He plays piano in a band on weekends.
